observed.note: Exact liquidation-cluster prices beyond the visible current labels are not stored because the screenshot resolution does not support reliable numeric extraction.

diagnosis: The previous long interpretation over-weighted elevated CVD and falling OI. Price failed to translate strong/aggressive-buy flow and leverage cleanup into durable upward structural repair. This is buyer inefficiency / passive-seller absorption, not a confirmed long edge.
liquidity_map_rule: Liquidation heatmaps are target/context maps, not directional entry signals. A nearby liquidity pool does not mean support or reversal. Direction must come from price response plus structure plus CVD/OI path.

edge_correction.old_bad_rule: CVD high/up + OI down => long allowed
edge_correction.new_rule: CVD high/up + OI down only arms a candidate. Long requires price to reclaim and accept value/structure after the flush. If price fails to respond proportionally, classify BUYER_INEFFICIENCY and do not add.
required_long_confirmation: holds or successfully retests the reclaimed level
CVD remains stable/up without a fresh collapse
OI does not expand aggressively against price progress
edge_correction.bearish_transition: If price continues lower while CVD weakens and OI starts rising, reclassify as fresh bearish leverage expansion.

risk_management_lesson: Do not keep passive buy limits active merely because OI is lower or a heatmap shows liquidity below. Remaining limits should be conditioned on live confirmation when the prior structure/reclaim has failed.
model_training_lesson: The edge is not predicting where liquidation heatmap bands sit; it is detecting whether real price response validates or falsifies order-flow effort. Price response must outrank indicator direction when they disagree.
